C_enumeratedSteps.detect: C fires when TWO OR MORE of its three independent sub-signals hold: C1 enumerated lines (^\s*(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s) >= 3; C2 distinct action verbs (add|build|change|check|implement|verify|设计|实现|验证|改造|补充) >= 3; C3 action clauses (>= 3 clauses that each pair an action verb with an object, whether or not numbered) >= 3.
C_enumeratedSteps.measure: count of C1, C2, C3; C is satisfied at >= 2 of 3
C_enumeratedSteps.revisionNote: SUPERSEDES the original literal wording ('C1 >= 3 OR C2 >= 3'). Measured contradiction: frozen complex prompt #1 ('Align the bundle with upstream: audit the orchestration surface, then implement the routing change.') has 2 enumerated lines and 2 action verbs, so the literal rule could never satisfy its own frozen complex side — while the frozen simple prompts must stay silent. The implemented form (C1/C2/C3 with a >= 2-of-3 majority) was accepted because it keeps BOTH frozen prompt sets falsifiable in practice: the two-sided case measures simple 3/3 silent and complex 3/3 triggering on a settled revision. Updating the prompts instead would have invalidated the evidence already produced against them.

items.name: node-level retry
items.assert: a terminal failed task can be retried without discarding the tasks that already completed

items.name: revision without re-running completed work
items.assert: amending a task definition re-runs ONLY the changed task and its TRANSITIVE DEPENDENTS. A completed node whose own definition is unchanged AND none of whose transitive dependencies were changed/added/xor-moved keeps its cached result — that is the 'completed nodes are not re-run' guarantee. A completed DEPENDENT of an amended task IS re-run, because its input changed (upstream amend semantics: the amended event carries invalidatedNodeIds); keeping a stale dependent result would be the bug, not the contract.
items.resolves: Planner R4F1 — the earlier wording 'and its dependents' read as conflicting with the user's 'amend must not re-run completed nodes'. The two are reconciled by scoping the no-re-run guarantee to nodes whose transitive inputs did not change.

t4Requirements.residualFieldGap: FINAL — THIS SECTION IS THE AUTHORITATIVE RULE SET; where it disagrees with any captain message or with any earlier revision of this field, THIS TEXT WINS. (a) Inputs: per-row seam booleans are DERIVABLE from raw/upstream-skill-records.json (harnessSeamChange = any seam trigger class present; binaryDependency = binaries > 0; credentialDependency = creds > 0). They are RECORD-ONLY; the single row absent from raw (skills-loader-core/security-research) takes the `unknown` fallback. (b) D3 RULE (deterministic, replaces every earlier band/value): `D3 = T + B`, where T = 1 if any SEAM TRIGGER class (envKeyOmo, teamTools, dagRunId, workflowTool) is present WITH mechanism evidence, else 0; and B = 1 if the row's own SKILL.md carries an executable command (`bun`, `node`, `npx`, `uv`, script paths) that is part of the porting work, else 0; the `unknown` fallback row uses D3 = 3. Non-trigger classes (taskTool, categoryRouting, cliOmo, omoDir, binaries, creds) NEVER add to D3 — they are annotation-only ('environment prerequisite: needs X'). (c) Class mapping is IDENTICAL to (b): SEAM TRIGGERS are the D3-relevant HARD set (envKeyOmo, teamTools, dagRunId, workflowTool); D4-band classes (soft) are categoryRouting, cliOmo, omoDir, taskTool, binaries, creds; there is no third band. (d) EVIDENCE QUALITY, taking precedence over (c): only a hit whose evidenceQuality = mechanism contributes to D4 — a prose hit is recorded but neither scored nor able to trigger V4 (measured prose-only: dev-browser 'workflow loop', frontend 'Design System and Component Workflow'; the frozen class table is CASE-SENSITIVE, so uppercase prose never entered a class). (e) V4 predicate: `(dagRunId ∧ mechanism) OR (envKeyOmo ∧ workflowTool ∧ mechanism)` ⇒ only omo-senpi/mass-ulw and omo-senpi/dag-library. (f) THRESHOLD: `total >= 15 ⇒ adapt-then-install`; `total < 15 ⇒ skip`; vetoes (V1 equivalent, V4 runner-replacement) apply BEFORE the threshold. `couplingMeasurement != none` caps D4 (D4 ≠ 3) and is never an action by itself. (g) RECOMPUTED SCORES under (a)-(f) with T+B — the gate recomputes these and does not quote them as frozen facts: remove-deadcode 13 (T=0 because its only hit is binaries/`bun`, a soft class; B=1) ⇒ skip; security-research 18 (T=1 teamTools = seam trigger; soft hit creds; B=0) ⇒ adapt AND it is the row the captain told the user would survive; tech-debt-audit 17 (T=0, B=1) ⇒ adapt; skills-loader-core/security-research 19 (unknown fallback D3=3) ⇒ adapt; skills-loader-core/git-master 15 (T=0 — omoDir/cliOmo are soft classes, its trigger set is empty; B=0) ⇒ adapt EXACTLY at the threshold and therefore marked threshold-borderline; omo-codex/rules, skills-loader-core/dev-browser, skills-loader-core/frontend, omo-senpi/dag-library, omo-senpi/mass-ulw ⇒ skip. ACTION SET = adapt 4 / skip 6. The user's three approved skills therefore resolve to: security-research adapt (borderline), tech-debt-audit adapt, remove-deadcode skip — and the last one is ALSO the subject of measurement task t19, so its row must carry the marker 'pending t19' until that empirical measurement lands. (h) `userApprovedOverrides` MUST list every user-approved skill whose action differs from the earlier preview, each with its score, the rule that produced it, and an explicit 'the user may confirm or withdraw' note. (i) Boundary adjudication to carry into the table: 'at exactly 15' counts as PASS ('>= 15'), and any row landing exactly there must be flagged as threshold-borderline. FAILURE MODE TO AVOID (measured this wave): a rule text, a derivation formula and pre-announced numbers drifted apart because the numbers were announced before the formula was fixed — so the gate must ALWAYS recompute and must quote its inputs, never a remembered total.
